Alex: Quick follow-up from the attention-kernel RFC meeting earlier — we agreed to pick a short list of concrete operational tasks to decide Triton vs CUTLASS for the shipping runtime. Putting notes + asks here so we can close action items this sprint.

Jisoo: Thanks. I pushed microbench results to the RFC PR (link in thread). High-level: Triton kernels win on short sequences and batch sizes <= 8, CUTLASS custom attention is better for long contexts + large throughput. There are some memory fragmentation edge cases on CUTLASS when KV caching is heavy.

Sam: Re: KV cache — can you call out the exact scenario? Is it per-request memory growth or fragmentation during GC?

Jisoo: It's fragmentation. On long-lived sessions with varied sequence lengths we see allocator never fully coalesce freed regions on CUTLASS path. Shows up as OOM on 24GB with sustained 8k windows. Not consistent in short runs.

Pat: Maintenance concern: CUTLASS custom kernels require more vendor-provided tuning and occasional patching when driver/SM changes. Triton gives us faster dev iteration (python-first) but the performance delta for our typical web-LLM workload (avg seq=512) is small. So ops cost matters.

Matt: Proposal: define a kernel-selection table with policies and a tiny shim API. The runtime picks kernel variant per model/route: e.g. {policy: latency|cost|stability, preferred: triton|cutlass, fallback: cutlass|triton}. Minimal interface: compute(qkv, mask, kv_cache_ptr) -> output + new_kv_ptr.

Alex: I like the policy table. We need explicit metrics to drive policy: p50/p99 token latency, tokens/sec, memory high-water, and repro rate for OOM. Also an owner for each integration.

Sam: Action: verify KV cache lifecycle with CUTLASS + our allocator. I'll run long-lived session stress tests on dedicated pool and report memory traces. Owner: Sam. ETA: Tue (3 business days).

Jisoo: Action: expand microbench matrix (batch, seq, quantization modes bf16/fp16/int8) and add driver + CUDA version sweep. Owner: Jisoo. ETA: Fri.

Pat: Action: ops cost estimate for maintaining CUTLASS kernels (on-call + release churn). I'll draft a short TCO note with resourcing assumptions. Owner: Pat. ETA: next Wed.

Matt: Action: propose a minimal kernel-shim API and a config format. I'll open a PR with interface + example policy YAML. Quick sketch: 
```yaml
kernel_policy:
  default:
    policy: stability
    preferred: triton
    fallback: cutlass
  high_throughput_route:
    policy: throughput
    preferred: cutlass
    fallback: triton
```
And shim: 
```cpp
struct KernelResult { void* kv_out; Tensor out; };
KernelResult run_attention(const AttentionArgs&);
```

Jisoo: Add a test vector for KV serialization compatibility between variants. That will catch subtle layout/endianness/ptr issues.

CI Bot: Heads up — we'll need kernel-level perf/regression tests. I can add a new job matrix in CI that runs microbenchmarks nightly across a subset of CUDA versions and a triton head image. It will take ~4h of infra to bootstrap.

Alex: Good. Let's keep the pilot scope tight: (1) selection table + shim API PR, (2) extended microbench with allocator traces, (3) CI nightly perf job, (4) TCO note. If those look good we can pick stable defaults and roll a canary to a small Dedicated pool.

Sam: Quick question on canary: do we want model-level pinning or route-level? For safety I'd vote route-level (so we can target only expensive routes).

Pat: Agreed route-level. Also add automatic fallback policy: if OOM or p99 regression > 2x, switch traffic to fallback variant for 10 minutes and create an alert.

Matt: I'll sketch the rollout plan in the PR: feature flag + route annotation + metric gating + automatic fallback.

Jisoo: I'll include a KV dump util to capture allocator maps. That should help reproduce the fragmentation.

Alex: Nice. Final: owners + deadlines recap in one message?

Matt: Owners recap: Sam -> allocator stress tests (ETA Tue). Jisoo -> expanded microbench + KV dump util (ETA Fri). Pat -> TCO/resourcing note (ETA next Wed). Matt -> kernel-shim API + policy PR + rollout sketch (ETA Thu). CI Bot -> nightly perf job (kickoff ETA Thu, infra ~4h).

Alex: Perfect. I'll file these as action items in the RFC PR and ping leads. Please add any blockers here. :thumbsup:
